messages.content: 你能使用lawsuit_search功能從加州的聖塔克拉拉檢索所有涉及實體“Google”的訴訟，然後再從加州的聖馬刁檢索涉及實體“Facebook”的訴訟嗎？

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Retrieve all lawsuits involving a particular entity from specified jurisdiction. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

county.description: The jurisdiction for the lawsuit search.

state.description: The state for the lawsuit search. Default is California.

The function signature: lawsuit_search(entity: string, county: string, state?: string). So we need to call with entity="Google", county="Santa Clara", state="California". Then entity="Facebook", county="San Mateo", state="California".

Then after we get the result, we call again for Facebook. But the user might expect us to do both calls in one go. But the guidelines say we can only output one function call at a time. So we will do the first call. Then we will wait for the function's response. Then we will call again. But the user specifically asked to retrieve both. So we can do the first call, then after we get the result, we can do the second call. That is acceptable.
